properties.description: Whether API keys for machine clients are on; `true` or `false` only, any other value fails startup.
properties.name: cosec.api-key.enabled

properties.description: Keys of the in-memory store, by their SHA-256 hash. Ignored with the Redis store.
properties.name: cosec.api-key.keys

properties.description: Where keys live: `memory` (the [keys] below) or `redis` (shared by every instance, needs `cosec-cocache`), under `<cosec.key-prefix>:api-key`.
properties.name: cosec.api-key.store

properties.description: Whether the audit log listener is on, and the Kafka audit listener with `cosec.audit.kafka.enabled`.
properties.name: cosec.audit.enabled

properties.description: `required` makes a permit wait for the broker's acknowledgement; best effort by default (RFC 0006 §9.2).
properties.name: cosec.audit.kafka.delivery

properties.description: Whether the Kafka audit listener is on; it needs `cosec-kafka` and a `KafkaOperations` bean.
properties.name: cosec.audit.kafka.enabled

properties.description: The Kafka topic of the audit events.
properties.name: cosec.audit.kafka.topic

properties.description: Whether the login beans are on, which turn credentials into a token; authenticating requests does not depend on it.
properties.name: cosec.authentication.login.enabled

properties.description: Where the starter serves `POST` of this route, such as `/auth/refresh`. Unset (the default), it is not served and the application serves its own.
properties.name: cosec.authentication.login.logout.path

properties.description: Where the starter serves `POST` of this route, such as `/auth/refresh`. Unset (the default), it is not served and the application serves its own.
properties.name: cosec.authentication.login.refresh.path

properties.description: Whether social login is on (`cosec-social`); it needs `cosec.authentication.login.enabled`.
properties.name: cosec.authentication.login.social.enabled

properties.description: The OAuth providers, one per name, each a JustAuth `AuthConfig` with its `type` and `client-id` required.
properties.name: cosec.authentication.login.social.registration

properties.description: Drops a local copy not read for this long. A number without a unit is seconds, as the expiry settings always were.
properties.name: cosec.authentication.revocation.cache.expire-after-access

properties.description: The initial capacity of the local copy; unset, CoCache's.
properties.name: cosec.authentication.revocation.cache.initial-capacity

properties.description: How long a local copy lives at most (CoCache's `localMaxAge`): the bound on staleness when an invalidation is lost.
properties.name: cosec.authentication.revocation.cache.local-max-age

properties.description: The most entries the local copy holds.
properties.name: cosec.authentication.revocation.cache.maximum-size

properties.description: Whether a request's token is refused (503) while the revocations cannot be read, instead of accepted: the documented exception to failing closed, which applies to verifying a token only. Refresh always fails then.
properties.name: cosec.authentication.revocation.fail-closed

properties.description: How long a check's two revocation reads may take together: past it the store is unavailable, so a request's token is accepted (or refused, with `fail-closed`) and a refresh fails. Positive, and less than `cosec.pipeline.authentication-timeout`, or a hanging store would make every authenticated request 503.
properties.name: cosec.authentication.revocation.read-timeout

properties.description: How much later than a subject revocation a token may have been issued and still be revoked by it: room for an issuer whose clock runs ahead of the revoking one.
properties.name: cosec.authentication.revocation.skew

properties.description: How long one call of the stage's collaborator may take, the stage being the group this property is under: `attributes` (an `AttributeProvider` that sets no timeout of its own; past it its attributes are unavailable) and `rate-limit` (the `RateLimiter`; past it the rule's `strictFailure` decides).
properties.name: cosec.authorization.attributes.timeout

properties.description: How long one call of the `MembershipProvider` may take; past it, or when it fails, the request is 503. The fill of the membership cache takes no longer than this.
properties.name: cosec.authorization.membership.timeout

properties.description: How long an instance remembers that the loader did not know a principal (a removed member's token still valid), so that its requests do not reach the loader each time. Zero remembers nothing; at most one minute, the default life of a cached membership. A principal added meanwhile is known when it ends, or at once on the instance that invalidated it. A failed load is never remembered.
properties.name: cosec.authorization.membership.unknown-ttl

properties.description: How long one call of the stage's collaborator may take, the stage being the group this property is under: `attributes` (an `AttributeProvider` that sets no timeout of its own; past it its attributes are unavailable) and `rate-limit` (the `RateLimiter`; past it the rule's `strictFailure` decides).
properties.name: cosec.authorization.rate-limit.timeout

properties.description: How many proxy hops of `X-Forwarded-For` to trust: `0` ignores the header (a directly exposed host), `N` takes the entry the closest of N trusted proxies appended.
properties.name: cosec.authorization.remote-ip.max-trusted-index

properties.description: The route maps WebFlux and WebMvc hosts load (RFC 0005 §5.3), comma-separated resource locations; a location that does not exist, or a map with no routes, fails startup. Unset, the host runs without a route map, every request in the `http` namespace, unless [DEFAULT_LOCATION] exists: then startup fails, so that a map someone shipped is never left out without a word. Empty runs without a route map on purpose.
properties.name: cosec.authorization.routes.location

properties.description: The app this host serves (RFC 0004 §4.6); unset when requests declare their app.
properties.name: cosec.authorization.scope.app-id

properties.description: Off, this instance takes no part in shadow windows: it reports no samples and no `CANDIDATE_ERROR`, so its traffic counts for nothing in a window.
properties.name: cosec.authorization.shadow.enabled

properties.description: The prefix of this instance's id in reports and statuses: the id is `<instance-id>.<suffix>`, the suffix new at every start, so that a restarted process never replaces its predecessor's reports; a random UUID when empty. Only letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-` (it ends a Redis key); any other id fails startup.
properties.name: cosec.authorization.shadow.instance-id

properties.description: How often this instance writes its reports and its status.
properties.name: cosec.authorization.shadow.report-interval

properties.description: The share of requests evaluated again on the candidates, from 0 to 1.
properties.name: cosec.authorization.shadow.sample-rate

properties.description: How long a request waits for a document that is not installed; past it the document counts as failed. Positive.
properties.name: cosec.authorization.snapshot.cold-load-timeout

properties.description: Threads that compile documents; positive.
properties.name: cosec.authorization.snapshot.compile-threads

properties.description: What a Redis whose `maxmemory-policy` is not `noeviction`, or cannot be read, does to startup (`SNP-3`).
properties.name: cosec.authorization.snapshot.eviction-check

properties.description: The lag beyond which the tenants above fail closed; not negative.
properties.name: cosec.authorization.snapshot.fail-closed.max-lag

properties.description: Tenants that must not be decided on old documents: a request of one is 503 unless a DENY matches, when the oldest document it reads was confirmed longer ago than `max-lag`.
properties.name: cosec.authorization.snapshot.fail-closed.tenants

properties.description: How long a document may go unconfirmed before it is logged at ERROR as stale.
properties.name: cosec.authorization.snapshot.lag-escalate

properties.description: How long a document may go unconfirmed before it is logged at WARN; not more than `lag-escalate`.
properties.name: cosec.authorization.snapshot.lag-warn

properties.description: How long an instance serves its local copy of a document before it asks Redis again; the one value for the snapshot cache's local tier, whatever a cache customizer or `cocache.*` property sets.
properties.name: cosec.authorization.snapshot.local-max-age

properties.description: The most app ids held as having no app document (positive, `SNP-7`). App ids come from requests, so this bounds what a client naming made-up apps makes an instance remember.
properties.name: cosec.authorization.snapshot.max-absent-apps

properties.description: The most tenant ids held as having no tenant document (positive, `SNP-7`), about 470 bytes each. Each request of such a tenant reads its entry: one dropped is read from Redis again on the tenant's next request.
properties.name: cosec.authorization.snapshot.max-absent-tenants

properties.description: The most app documents held in memory (positive); the least recently used one is dropped beyond it.
properties.name: cosec.authorization.snapshot.max-apps

properties.description: The most tenant documents held in memory (positive); the platform document is never dropped. About 30 KB each for a tenant document of 5 roles of 20 permissions and 20 bindings: size the heap for it.
properties.name: cosec.authorization.snapshot.max-tenants

properties.description: App documents loaded at startup, after the platform document; readiness waits for them.
properties.name: cosec.authorization.snapshot.prewarm-apps

properties.description: Whether the apps this host names are loaded at startup, as `prewarm-apps` are, and held (`SNP-20`): its `cosec.authorization.scope.app-id`, and on a gateway every `cosec-app-id` its routes name, then every app a refreshed route names. Off, they load on their first request, as before.
properties.name: cosec.authorization.snapshot.prewarm-host-apps

properties.description: Tenant documents loaded at startup, after the platform document; readiness waits for them.
properties.name: cosec.authorization.snapshot.prewarm-tenants

properties.description: Documents a revalidation pass confirms at once (positive). A pass takes about the documents held × one conditional read ÷ this; past `revalidate-interval`, passes run back to back and lag grows with them.
properties.name: cosec.authorization.snapshot.reload-concurrency

properties.description: How often a pass starts that confirms every installed document against Redis; while a pass is still in flight, the next starts as soon as it ends. A change whose invalidation was lost is installed by the first pass that reaches its document (`SNP-6`). At least 1 second, at most 5 minutes, less than `lag-warn` and, with fail-closed tenants, less than `fail-closed.max-lag`; anything else fails startup.
properties.name: cosec.authorization.snapshot.revalidate-interval

properties.description: The services' route maps, comma-separated resource locations (UC-1): the control plane lists, for a change, the `http:` DENY statements and rate limit rules a mapped route escapes. Unset, nothing is compared, and the change says so. Each host's own WARN needs only its own route map, not this.
properties.name: cosec.control.analysis.route-maps

properties.description: The app control-plane actions are authorized in (RFC 0007 §7.2).
properties.name: cosec.control.app-id

properties.description: How long an approval stays valid; startup fails when it is longer than `cosec.jwt.token-validity.refresh`, how long a token revocation is kept.
properties.name: cosec.control.approval.expire-after

properties.description: Whether the trust root's own changes are analyzed too (RFC 0007 Q10): what the analysis cannot prove needs a second administrator's approval. A change that escalates needs one either way.
properties.name: cosec.control.approval.four-eyes

properties.description: `required` makes publishing and break-glass wait for the broker; break-glass needs one REQUIRED listener.
properties.name: cosec.control.audit.kafka.delivery

properties.description: Whether the Kafka change listener is on; it needs `cosec-kafka` and a `KafkaOperations` bean.
properties.name: cosec.control.audit.kafka.enabled

properties.description: The Kafka topic of the change events.
properties.name: cosec.control.audit.kafka.topic

properties.description: How long every REQUIRED change listener together may take to record a gated step before it fails (503).
properties.name: cosec.control.audit.required-timeout

properties.description: The longest a break-glass binding may last; at most 24 hours.
properties.name: cosec.control.break-glass.max-duration

properties.description: An open change request expires this long after it was proposed.
properties.name: cosec.control.changes.expire-after

properties.description: Whether this instance runs the control plane, when `cosec-control` and `cosec-cocache` are on its classpath. `false` leaves it out, and the instance reads the policy documents and candidates read-only (SNP-18): a fleet that ships one image for both roles sets it on the data-plane role. `true` or `false` only.
properties.name: cosec.control.enabled

properties.description: Where the control API is served (RFC 0007 §10.2): its routes are under `{base-path}/v1`.
properties.name: cosec.control.http.base-path

properties.description: The largest request body the control routes read, on WebMvc and WebFlux alike; a larger one is answered 400 (CTL-41). A document's 8 MB cap (RFC 0003 Q14) and room for the operations' JSON around it.
properties.name: cosec.control.http.max-body-size

properties.description: The revisions always kept per document; older ones are reclaimed once also older than `min-age`.
properties.name: cosec.control.revisions.max-count

properties.description: Revisions younger than this are always kept.
properties.name: cosec.control.revisions.min-age

properties.description: The records of conflicted publishes are removed once this old.
properties.name: cosec.control.revisions.orphan-age

properties.description: How often each instance tries to reclaim; one instance at a time does each document.
properties.name: cosec.control.revisions.reclaim-interval

properties.description: How often shadowing changes are looked at, by one instance at a time; a window closes up to this late.
properties.name: cosec.control.shadow.check-interval

properties.description: A window closes at this age with fewer samples, as insufficient evidence; not less than `min-duration`.
properties.name: cosec.control.shadow.max-duration

properties.description: A shadow window closes no earlier than this, once it also has `min-samples`.
properties.name: cosec.control.shadow.min-duration

properties.description: The compared samples a window needs to close before `max-duration`.
properties.name: cosec.control.shadow.min-samples

properties.description: The CosId generator whose ids CoSec takes, with its codec; CosId's `default` unless set.
properties.name: cosec.cosid.generator

properties.description: Whether CoSec's auto-configurations are on at all; the unknown-key check and a gateway's identity strip hold anyway.
properties.name: cosec.enabled

properties.description: The token claims forwarded besides the identity, such as `name` and `email`: strings, numbers, booleans.
properties.name: cosec.gateway.identity.claims

properties.description: Whether a gateway forwards the verified identity: to a `lb://` route, or a route with metadata `cosec-identity: true`; never to one with `cosec-identity: false` (RC1-49).
properties.name: cosec.gateway.identity.enabled

properties.description: Whether the client's credentials still go downstream, to the routes that receive the identity: the `Authorization` header, the API key header (`cosec.pipeline.api-key-header`) and the `authorization` query parameter (RC1-5). Off: a service behind needs none. Turn it on only for services that verify the token again or call other APIs on the user's behalf.
properties.name: cosec.gateway.identity.forward-authorization

properties.description: A larger identity fails the request closed (500) rather than being cut.
properties.name: cosec.gateway.identity.max-size

properties.description: Actuator endpoints that may be exposed over HTTP on the gateway's application port, where CoSec does not authorize them, because something else protects them. Any other one but `health` fails startup (`STA-2`, RC1-48); `gateway`, which writes routes, is never accepted here.
properties.name: cosec.gateway.unprotected-endpoints

properties.description: Whether the `ext.ip2region.*` attribute provider is on (`cosec-ip2region`).
properties.name: cosec.ip2region.enabled

properties.description: Where the IPv6 `.xdb` database is (a Spring resource location, `file:` or `classpath:`), loaded beside the bundled IPv4 one. Unset, an IPv6 client's region is unavailable: a DENY on it is Indeterminate, never skipped (round 2 M5). A location that does not exist fails startup.
properties.name: cosec.ip2region.ipv6-location

properties.description: The signing algorithm; issuers and verifiers must agree.
properties.name: cosec.jwt.algorithm

properties.description: Whether JWTs are issued, verified and revoked; unset, on where the host verifies tokens itself and off behind a gateway.
properties.name: cosec.jwt.enabled

properties.description: The signing secret, required while JWT is enabled: startup fails when it is blank or shorter than the algorithm needs in UTF-8 bytes (32 for hmac256, 48 for hmac384, 64 for hmac512).
properties.name: cosec.jwt.secret

properties.description: How long a session lasts from its login, however often it is refreshed; then the user signs in again.
properties.name: cosec.jwt.session.lifetime

properties.description: How the starter's refresh route gives a refreshed token its memberships (its roles and attached policies), when the application declares no `MembershipRefresh` bean: no default, and with the route served startup fails until this is `from-token`, the statement that a refreshed token keeps the memberships of the token it replaces, so a removed role or attached policy applies at the member's next sign-in, `lifetime` at the latest (`STA-8`).
properties.name: cosec.jwt.session.memberships-on-refresh

properties.description: How long after a refresh the pair it replaced is answered at the current generation: the window a client has to retry a refresh whose response it lost.
properties.name: cosec.jwt.session.rotation-leeway

properties.description: The lifetime of an access token.
properties.name: cosec.jwt.token-validity.access

properties.description: The lifetime of a refresh token; a revocation is kept this long, plus one second.
properties.name: cosec.jwt.token-validity.refresh

properties.description:
The prefix of every Redis key this deployment writes (`SNP-9`, RC1-46): snapshot documents, control-plane records, shadow reports, token revocations, memberships (`

:snapshot:…`, `

:control:…`, `

:token:…`, …), API keys (`

:api-key:…`) and rate limit counters (`

:rate-limiter:…`). Two deployments on one Redis that differ in it share nothing. A trailing `:` is ignored.
properties.name: cosec.key-prefix

properties.description: Whether the metrics listener is on; it needs `cosec-micrometer` and a `MeterRegistry` bean.
properties.name: cosec.metrics.enabled

properties.description: On shutdown, how long queued events still go out before the rest is dropped.
properties.name: cosec.observability.listener.drain-timeout

properties.description: The events one BEST_EFFORT listener may have waiting; a full queue drops the next and counts it.
properties.name: cosec.observability.listener.queue-capacity

properties.description: How long one REQUIRED listener may take; past it a permit becomes 503.
properties.name: cosec.observability.listener.required-timeout

properties.description: Whether the bearer-auth customizer of the OpenAPI document is on (`cosec-openapi`).
properties.name: cosec.openapi.enabled

properties.description: Whether a token may come in the `authorization` cookie; off, since a browser sends a cookie on its own, on a cross-site request too. Turn it on only with your own CSRF defense.
properties.name: cosec.pipeline.allow-cookie-token

properties.description: Whether a token may come in the query string; off, since URLs end up in logs.
properties.name: cosec.pipeline.allow-query-token

properties.description: The header an API key comes in. No document may read it (`CND-5`, [credentialHeaders]).
properties.name: cosec.pipeline.api-key-header

properties.description: Authenticating the request's credentials.
properties.name: cosec.pipeline.authentication-timeout

properties.description: An identity older than this (plus `cosec.authentication.revocation.skew`) is refused: 401 `token-expired`.
properties.name: cosec.pipeline.identity.max-age

properties.description: A larger header is refused: 400 `invalid-request`.
properties.name: cosec.pipeline.identity.max-size

properties.description: The statement that only the gateway can reach this service (`STA-7`). A service in `gateway` mode believes any `CoSec-Identity` it receives, a header with no signature, so whoever else can reach it is whoever they claim to be. No default: the mode does not start until this is `true`, written by an operator who has made it so (a NetworkPolicy that admits the gateway's pods only, mutual TLS, a private network).
properties.name: cosec.pipeline.identity.only-gateway-can-reach

properties.description: `enforce` decides with policies; `gateway` trusts the identity the gateway in front forwards (`CoSec-Identity`).
properties.name: cosec.pipeline.mode

properties.description: The whole evaluation of one request; past it the request is answered 503.
properties.name: cosec.pipeline.timeout

properties.description: How much of an evaluation's trace decision events carry.
properties.name: cosec.pipeline.trace-level

properties.description: Permitted level of access for the cosecServiceGenerator endpoint.
properties.name: management.endpoint.cosec-service-generator.access
